title: Nevermore
essence: One trail followed twice, each time ending in a body part taken back and sworn over. On a night shore of ash and tambourine pieces, a man in red and black with his hands in his pockets and a hollow chest finds his own heart throbbing in the sand; it floats up and re-enters him, and he says nevermore. He follows it up an incline into a moonlit garden where faith scatters as mustard seeds and golden blooms turn to face him, and in the deepest dark he finds his two hands palm-down on bare ground, puts them back on, stands, and says it again.
palette_notes: Night navy and moon silver come from 3da7e92e (the moon, used in the film cut) and ee11f371 (the night garden). Ash greys (#8c9aa6) from the shore. #c23a2c is the costume's red piping and the red bare ground of 7a904269, where the hands are found. #d9a640 is the golden hue of the blooms and the mustard seeds. #5aa7ff is the suite's one accent and in this film it belongs only to the heart's pulse: never the moon, never the blooms. #e8e4d8 is the paper of the vow word cut out of the dark.

full_text.line: What if I follow this trail to where the broken pieces have washed ashore and the ashes of expired wildfires
cover sands and debris
lift it from the night seawater's floor.
The waves will calm to fold it whispers and the winds will mute the trees for the right level of silence
to find a throbbing heart left at the midlife corner returned toward the incline.
A familiar heart
which has shaken off every sad blue note life can perform
to overcome and spread inspiration
and it used to be mine. I'll lift it with care putting it back in place and tell myself
nevermore.
What if I follow this reclaimed heart to where the puzzle pieces of faith are handcrafted
scrambled and scattered as mustard seas into the vast moonlight night's field.
The plants in a golden hue bloom and face toward me in anticipation.
The weeds repel falling into the shadows where our memories hide and mean so little in moments of defeat
as I'm called forward.
The clouds meet the stars for the deepest level of darkness welcoming extra hard work
to search for the bare ground for two hands. Hands that once could tusk dusk after dusk
find and celebrate a new life and feel good
and they too used to be mine.
I put them back on with the care of my future at stake and say to myself
nevermore. I've wanted the world and lost my soul.
I want nothing more than to just be myself and nothing more
and be alright. I do believe I'll be alright.
This reclaimed and dust settled heart rediscovered but dusted hands remind me
but say to me in this still muted tree in night garden feels silence
nevermore.
Now go.

insights: Hands in pockets is a casting gift: the arm cards end at the pocket, so the first four movements need no hand animation at all, and the reveal of empty sleeves costs one replacement.
Build the poem as two identical arcs in inverted material: the first half is ink on paper, the second paper cut out of ink. Reuse the trail, the kneel and the vow, only invert them.
Give the suite accent to the heart and nothing else; a second blue mark (moon, blooms) would steal it.
Never let the heart overshoot: it travels slowly and ends exactly at the chest, or the move reads as pointing.
The darkness only goes one way: dusk shore, moonlit field, deepest dark. Do not relight the field at the end; let the reach pool widen instead.
The hands must be a palm slab with short fingers, a thumb and a wrist stub; radiating fingers read as a starfish.
future: The red/black outfit with sunglasses starts here and is POET's costume through 14.
The night garden field is where 05's ancestors' parade arrives; POET walks out of it.
The reclaimed heart with its blue pulse can sit in the chest in every later poem as continuity.
The detachable hands answer 05's 'their blood flows through my hands'.
The raven cards are reusable for any later night exterior.
